A map of the repository, the decisions that shape it, and the mechanics behind the rules the guide states without explaining. Nothing here is needed to build a page. The working rules for contributors -- headers, style, the release checklist -- are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md); the deeper "why" behind each invariant, written as instructions for someone editing the code, is in [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/CLAUDE.md).

## Layout

```
_extensions/mathviz/   the Quarto extension: _extension.yml, mathviz.lua, dist/ (copied by the build)
dist/                  the generated bundle, committed (jsDelivr serves it by tag); never hand-edited
src/manifest.mjs       THE load order, for the build and the tests
src/js/<category>/     one VM.<category>.<name> per file; tests colocated as <name>.test.js
src/css/               tokens.css first, then one file per concern
src/chrome/            the opt-in site chrome: one .js + .css per piece (category-cloud.js has no .css), plus site.js (shared helpers); not in the bundle
src/fonts/             fonts.css and the self-hosted Inter / JetBrains Mono woff2 files
src/theme/theme.scss   template the build fills into dist/theme/mathviz-{light,dark}.scss
scripts/               build.mjs (concatenate + syntax-check), load-vm.mjs (test loader), release.mjs
docs/                  this site
starter/               the clone-and-go site; its _extensions/mathviz/ is mirrored in by the build
kit/                   what a consumer site copies in: the update hook
```

## One global, many small files

Every file under `src/js` is an IIFE that adds one member (occasionally two or three that belong together) to `window.VM`:

```js
(function attachVM(globalThis) {
  /** JSDoc … */
  const simpsonEstimate = (f, lo, hi, n) => { … }

  Object.assign((globalThis.VM ??= {}).numerical ??= {}, {simpsonEstimate})
})(window)
```

Members are added to the existing `VM` and namespace objects in place, never by replacing them, so a reference taken early (`const plotting = VM.plotting`, or the opt-in chrome scripts' `VM.chrome`) still sees every member added later.

The in-place merge means files can load in any order *as far as attaching goes*; the manifest exists for the few real load-time dependencies (every `*Pmf`/`*Pdf` reads `logGamma`; the `discreteMath` color helpers read `VM.plotting`; the SVG fullscreen button reuses the Plotly button's icon). `mustPrecede` in `src/manifest.mjs` records them and `src/manifest.test.js` enforces them, along with "every file on disk is listed exactly once".

## The build is a concatenation, then a minify

`scripts/build.mjs` reads the manifest, joins the files with a separator, syntax-checks the result with `node --check` and writes `dist/mathviz.{js,css}` -- the readable bundle, with `// ---- src/js/… ----` markers and every comment, JSDoc included. It then minifies both with esbuild (the build's one dependency; no bundling, no syntax lowering) into `dist/mathviz.min.{js,css}`, plus `dist/mathviz.min.js.map`, a source map that embeds the readable source, so a stack trace or a devtools breakpoint in a consumer's browser still lands on a recognizable file. Comments are over 70% of the readable bundle: 289 kB becomes 64 kB. The minified pair and the map are copied into `_extensions/mathviz/dist/` (the extension loads only those), and the whole extension is mirrored into `starter/_extensions/mathviz/` (what `quarto add` would install there), so the starter is committed working and tracks the working tree.

The one subtlety is the separator. For JS it is a lone `;`. Each file ends in a call -- `})(window)`, or `})()` for a module with nothing to export -- and two of those back to back parse as `})(window)(function …)`: the first file's return value called with the second file as its argument. That is syntactically valid, so `node --check` can't catch it, and the page dies after the first file with `(intermediate value)(...) is not a function`. The semicolon makes each file its own statement.

`dist/` is committed because both distribution channels serve the repository as-is: `quarto add` downloads an archive and runs nothing, and jsDelivr serves files straight from a tag. CI rebuilds and fails on a diff, so `src/` and `dist/` can't drift.

## Tests run the real files

`scripts/load-vm.mjs` evaluates every manifest entry, in order, into the Node process's global scope (indirect `eval`, so the IIFEs see a `window`), with a minimal `document` and `Plotly` stub for the modules that touch them at load time. The `*.test.js` files import it and test `VM.*` -- the production code, not re-implementations. `node --test` finds them; The dev dependencies are math.js, for the expression tests, esbuild for the build, and Playwright for `npm run test:layout`.

Two tests guard the documentation itself: `manifest.test.js` (above) and `docs-coverage.test.js`, which fails if any `VM.*` member lacks a `### VM.<category>.<name>` heading in `docs/reference/`, or a heading names something that doesn't exist.

## The version is in three places

`package.json`, `_extensions/mathviz/_extension.yml` and `VERSION` in `mathviz.lua`. The build refuses to run unless they agree. The Lua one names the `site_libs/quarto-contrib/mathviz-<version>/` folder in a consumer's output, which is what busts their browser cache on upgrade.

## The Lua filter's odd shape

`mathviz.lua` adds **one HTML dependency per vendor `<script>` tag** (`mathviz-mathjs`, `mathviz-plotly`, `mathviz-referrer`), each *before* the `mathviz` dependency that carries the bundle. Three facts about Quarto's dependency handling, verified against Quarto 1.7's source, force this:

1. `quarto.doc.include_text("in-header", …)` lands in `header-includes`, which is emitted *below* the whole dependency block -- so a Plotly tag added that way loads after `mathviz.js`, and the patch finds no `Plotly` to patch.
2. Within one dependency, `scripts` entries are emitted before the `head` string, so the vendor tags can't share the bundle's dependency.
3. Quarto's `injectHtml` iterates a *live* `children` collection while moving nodes out of it, so a `head` string holding several tags loses every second one. One tag per dependency is the workaround.

`scripts`/`stylesheets` entries must be local files (Quarto copies them into `site_libs`), hence raw `<script>` tags in `head` for the CDN URLs. A head-only dependency creates no `site_libs` folder.

**Everything is deferred, vendors only where OJS is.** The two vendor tags carry `defer`, and so does the bundle (a `scripts` entry may be `{path, attribs = {defer = ""}}`). Deferred scripts and module scripts run in one list, in document order, after parsing: math.js, Plotly, the bundle, then Quarto's OJS runtime module, which Quarto emits below the dependency block. So the Plotly patch is in place before the first cell can draw, and nothing blocks the first paint -- Plotly alone is ~3.5 MB. The bundle can't stay synchronous behind deferred vendors: it would install the patch only at `DOMContentLoaded`, and an OJS cell can run before that. The vendor tags go only on pages with OJS cells (unless the option is `true` or a URL): the filter is a `Pandoc` function, not `Meta`, so it can walk the document, and by the time a project's filters run Quarto has compiled the page's `{ojs}` cells into a `<script type="ojs-module-contents">` raw block -- what it looks for, along with the `{ojs}` code blocks themselves for a project that orders its filters ahead of Quarto's.

**Options are two keys, merged by the filter.** Quarto merges a page's front matter into the project config key by key only for keys it knows. For any other key, `mathviz:` included, the page's value replaces the project's whole map (checked on Quarto 1.10.19). So the filter reads two keys: the project's `mathviz:` and the page's `mathviz-page:`, and `mergedOptions` lays the second over the first, one top-level key at a time. Every option is read from that merged table. The fixture's `cards.qmd` turns its cloud on this way, and `npm run test:layout` checks that the page still has the referrer meta, fonts and sidebar search from `_quarto.yml`.

## Token specificity {#token-specificity}

The CSS reads the `--vm-*` tokens the ordinary way; the JavaScript reads them with `getComputedStyle` **at call time**, so a chart built after a theme toggle sees the new values.

The defaults live in [`src/css/tokens.css`](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/src/css/tokens.css), and every one of them is wrapped in `:where()`, which has **zero specificity**. That is why a plain `:root { --vm-x: … }` in a consumer's stylesheet wins no matter which file loads first. It matters in Quarto specifically: an extension's stylesheet is injected **before** a project's `css:` files but **after** its compiled theme SCSS, so without `:where()` the library's `:root` block would beat a theme's own `:root` declarations. Don't unwrap them if you fork the CSS.

## Dark-mode detection {#dark-mode-detection}

Two places hold the dark-mode selector list and must stay identical: the `:where(…)` block in `src/css/tokens.css`, and `settings.darkSelector` in `src/js/plotting/chart-theme.js`. The CSS half declares the dark tokens; the JS half decides `themeName()` by testing the list against `<body>` and then `<html>`.

**Root-scoped on purpose.** A bare `[data-bs-theme="dark"]` looks equivalent to `html[data-bs-theme="dark"], body[data-bs-theme="dark"]` but isn't: Quarto sets that attribute directly on its `<nav>` to force a dark navbar on an otherwise-light page, and custom properties inherit down the DOM -- so an unscoped match painted the entire dark palette into the navbar (shipped in v0.1.0, fixed in v0.1.1). Match on `html` or `body` only, including in a `configure({darkSelector})` override.

**JS reads from `<body>`, never `<html>`.** The light tokens are declared on `:root`, but the dark ones under selectors that match `<body>` (Quarto flips a body class). So `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` returns the **light** value even in dark mode. Every `--vm-*` read in the library goes through `document.body`; if you write your own token-reading code, do the same. This exact mistake once turned every chart tooltip into a white box on the dark theme.

**Toggles are two steps.** Quarto's toggle flips the body class and swaps the stylesheet as **separate steps**, class first. A callback that reads tokens synchronously on the class change sees the outgoing theme's values. [`onThemeChange`](plotting.qmd#onThemeChange) waits two animation frames before notifying for exactly this reason, and compares the theme name inside that wait so unrelated body-class changes (a sidebar opening) don't fire it. Use it rather than your own `MutationObserver`.

## Self-installing modules

Slider playback, the draggable legend, the SVG fullscreen button and the slider-track fill share a pattern: one shared watcher, [`VM.ui.whenAdded`](ui.qmd#whenAdded) -- a single `MutationObserver` on `document.body` that re-queries each registered selector at most once per animation frame -- plus delegated document-level listeners, so they enhance elements Observable Inputs creates at runtime and recreates on every upstream change -- there is no single moment at which "all the sliders exist" to wire them up individually. (Each used to run its own observer, three of them querying every added node synchronously, which a Plotly redraw does thousands of times.) Each marks what it has enhanced (`data-vm-play-ready`, `data-vm-draggable`) to stay idempotent. `plotly-fullscreen-button.js` does the same job for Plotly by wrapping `Plotly.newPlot`/`react`, since there is no DOM to watch before the chart exists.

## Draggable points {#draggable-points}

[`draggablePoints`](plotting.qmd#draggablePoints) lays real elements over the chart (`.vm-drag-layer`, absolutely positioned over the div, which gets `.vm-drag-host` for `position: relative`) rather than drawing Plotly markers: that is what gives each point a keyboard, an accessible name and a focus ring, and lets it move at the pointer's rate without a redraw.

- **Pixels to data** go through the axis objects in `gd._fullLayout` (`_offset`, `_length`, `d2l`/`l2p`/`p2l`/`l2d`), so log, reversed and `scaleanchor` axes work. Nothing reads Plotly's drag-layer DOM. These are the same internals [`lockedAxes`](plotting.qmd#lockedAxes) reads, kept in one file.
- **Placement** is redone on `plotly_afterplot`, `plotly_relayout` and `plotly_relayouting`, which cover a resize, a theme toggle, fullscreen and a zoom.
- **Theme:** a point's color is a CSS value (a `var(--vm-color-*)` by default), so a toggle recolors it without re-running the `viewof` cell, which would reset it.
- **Touch:** only the points have `touch-action: none`. A touch elsewhere on the chart scrolls the page, so a full-width chart can't trap a phone reader. The pad (`jump` or `add`) keeps the default `touch-action` and moves or adds a point on a tap; a swipe arrives as `pointercancel` and does nothing.
- **Ending a drag:** the pointer is captured on the point (or the pad), and the drag ends on `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture`, or a `pointermove` with `buttons === 0`. The last two catch a release that never arrived, which would otherwise leave the point following a mouse with no button held.
- **Focus:** a press on a point isn't cancelled, so the browser's own press-focus hands it the keyboard without a focus ring. A press on the pad focuses the moved or added point with `focusVisible: false`.
- **Adding and removing:** `add` and `remove` rebuild every point (the pad sits under them, so a press on a point drags it rather than adding one), which renumbers the default labels; array `label`/`color` entries are spliced out with a removed point, so the others keep theirs. A mouse press that adds keeps dragging the new point, and its release fires the one `"change"`.
- **Re-running** the cell on the same chart detaches the earlier points first (`gd.__vmDragPoints`): their layer, DOM listeners (one `AbortController`) and Plotly listeners.

## Generated classes {#generated-classes}

The library writes these itself; a page never authors them.

| Class / property | Written by |
|---|---|
| `ojs-legend-overlay`, `ojs-legend-item`, `ojs-legend-swatch` | `VM.ui.legendOverlay` |
| `vm-static-key`, `vm-static-key-item` | `VM.ui.staticKey` (its swatch SVGs are excluded from the SVG fullscreen button's figure and from centering) |
| `vm-overlay-grip`, `vm-overlay-dragging`, `data-vm-draggable` | the draggable-legend module |
| `vm-play`, `vm-play-button`, `vm-play-more`, `vm-play-panel`, `vm-play-group`, `vm-play-pills`, `vm-play-pill`, `vm-play-pill-on`, `vm-playing`, `vm-has-play`, `data-vm-play-ready` | slider playback |
| `vm-fullscreen-toggle`, `vm-fs-figure` | the SVG fullscreen button |
| `vm-drag-host`, `vm-drag-layer`, `vm-drag-pad`, `vm-drag-point`, `vm-drag-active` | `VM.plotting.draggablePoints`: the chart div, the layer over it, the `jump`/`add` pad, each point, the point being dragged |
| `ojs-table-toolbar`, `ojs-table-container` | `VM.ui.renderTable` |
| `vm-stat-row`, `vm-stat`, `vm-stat-label`, `vm-stat-value`, `--vm-stat-count` | `VM.ui.statRow` (the count caps the row at 14rem per tile) |
| `vm-embed`, `vm-app-active`, `vm-sidebar-search`, `vm-sidebar-search-empty`, `vm-sidebar-search-hidden`, `vm-share-*`, `vm-report-bug-popup`, `vm-category-cloud`, `category--all`, `data-vm-cloud-ready` | the opt-in [site extras](#site-extras) |
| `--sx`, `--vm-plot-aspect-ratio`, `--vm-fs-plot-width`, `--vm-svg-aspect`, `--vm-swatch` | runtime layout state: a slider's fill fraction, fullscreen letterboxing, a swatch's tint |

`vm-dark` is neither: it is a **theme hook** you may put on `<html>` or `<body>` to tell the library your site is in dark mode -- see [Theming](../theming.qmd#dark-mode). It styles nothing by itself.

## Host markup the CSS depends on {#host-markup}

Quarto OJS is the primary host, and several rules target markup mathviz doesn't own. They are harmless elsewhere, but on a non-Quarto page the corresponding behaviour is simply absent:

| Selector | What it fixes |
|---|---|
| `.cell-output-display`, `[id^="ojs-cell-"]` | Quarto wraps every OJS output in a scroll container (`overflow: auto`). The legend rules set `overflow: visible` on the ones inside a chart block, or the floating legend would be clipped to a zero-height box. The same clip is why the playback popover is a top-layer `[popover]`. |
| `.quarto-layout-cell { min-width: 0; max-width: 100% }` | lets a chart in a `layout-ncol` column shrink with it, and keeps each cell inside the screen when Quarto stacks the columns on a phone |
| `form[class^="oi-"]` | Observable Inputs' generated forms carry a hashed class. The panel rules override their fixed `360px` width and `120px` label column, and theme their buttons. Observable injects its own `.oi-<hash>` rules into `<head>` at runtime, *after* any stylesheet, so a mathviz rule that ties on specificity loses silently -- the shipped rules out-specify them or use `!important`. Bear this in mind if you add rules of your own. |
| `svg[class^="plot-"] { background: none }` | Observable Plot styles its SVG `background: white`, which stays white on the dark theme. Quarto clears it inline, but only on an SVG that is a cell's direct output, so a Plot wrapped in a `<div>` (a chart with a key under it) kept the white box. The attribute selector outranks Plot's single generated `.plot-<hash>` class. A Plot given its own `className` isn't matched. |
| `.js-plotly-plot .modebar*` | Plotly's modebar DOM; the pill, blur and hover-fade live here |

With plain `<input>`s in a `<div class="ojs-panel ojs-row">` everything panel-related still works -- the `form[class^="oi-"]` rules just find nothing to match.

## Site extras {#site-extras}

The pieces on [Site extras](../site.qmd) sit beside the bundle, not inside it. The build copies `src/chrome/`, `src/fonts/` and the generated `dist/theme/` into `_extensions/mathviz/{chrome,fonts,theme}/`, and none of them reaches `mathviz.js` or `mathviz.css`.

**One dependency per piece.** For each option that is set, `mathviz.lua` adds a dependency of its own (`mathviz-sidebar-search`, `mathviz-category-cloud`, `mathviz-embed`, `mathviz-share`, `mathviz-report-bug`, `mathviz-fonts`), so a site loads only what it turned on. `share` and `report-bug` also pull in `mathviz-chrome-site` (`chrome/site.js`), which defines the shared helpers under `VM.chrome`; Quarto emits it once however many ask. `share` adds `VM.chrome.share` and `sidebar-search` adds `VM.chrome.sidebarSearch` (`normalize` and `matches`, for `sidebar-search.test.js`) the same way. Every `VM.chrome` member exists only on a page whose site turned that piece on, so the [reference](index.qmd), which documents the bundle, doesn't list them.

**Settings travel as meta tags.** A filter can't template a script, so each option's values become `<meta name="mathviz:…">` tags, one per dependency for the injector bug [above](#the-lua-filters-odd-shape): `mathviz:share-site-url`, `mathviz:share-embed-docs`, `mathviz:report-bug-repo`, `mathviz:report-bug-branch`. The scripts read them at run time. A filter also can't see project config such as `website.site-url` (Quarto keeps it out of a page's metadata), which is why `share.site-url` repeats it.

**Embed mode runs first.** `embed.js` is a synchronous `<head>` script, so it puts `vm-embed` on `<html>` before anything paints, and every other chrome script checks for that class and skips itself. On `DOMContentLoaded` it marks the chosen block `vm-app-active`; `embed.css` then shows only that block, its descendants and its ancestors (Quarto wraps a `##` section in a `<section>`, so an app is not always a direct child of the content column). An id no `.vm-app` carries falls back to the first. It also wraps `history.replaceState` so a page that rebuilds its query string from scratch can't drop `embed`.

**Paths are site-relative.** Share links and the Report bug source link need the page's path from the site root, not `location.pathname`, which carries a prefix when the site is served below the root (a GitHub Pages project site, a local server over the repository). `VM.chrome.siteRelativePath` resolves Quarto's `quarto:offset` meta against the page to find the root as served and strips it. Report bug then maps `…/` or `….html` to the `.qmd` beside it, which holds for a project rendered from the repository root.

**The category cloud binds "All" itself.** `category-cloud.js` moves Quarto's `.quarto-listing-category` into a `<div class="vm-category-cloud">` above the first grid, default or table listing, removes the margin sidebar's "Categories" heading (and the sidebar, once empty, swapping `<main>`'s `column-page-left` for `column-page`), and prepends a `.category.category--all` entry with an empty `data-category`. It ships no stylesheet (the filter's `chrome()` helper takes a script-only flag): each site styles its own cloud. `quarto-listing.js` attaches its click handlers on `DOMContentLoaded`, and Quarto's scripts come before the extension's in `<head>`, so its listener has already run when this one does; the new entry's click goes through Quarto's public `window.quartoListingCategory("")` instead. An empty `data-category` is what Quarto's own `activateCategory("")` looks up (`btoa("")` is `""`), so "All" takes `.active` when the filter is cleared, and the script gives it `.active` at load when no entry has it. Every entry gets `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"`, and one `keydown` listener on the cloud turns Enter and Space into a `click()`; they stay divs so no browser button styles reach a site's cloud CSS. Quarto pushes a history entry per pick, and the listing page's inline script re-runs `quarto-listing-loaded` on `hashchange`, which re-applies the hash's category but skips an empty one, so Back to a page with no category (or to the `#category=` "All" leaves) kept the old filter; a `hashchange` listener here clears it when the hash names no category, by marking "All" active and calling `filter()` on each List.js instance in Quarto's `window["quarto-listings"]` -- not `quartoListingCategory("")`, which would push an entry and drop the Forward history. Any other hash (a footnote, a heading's anchor) is an in-page link and leaves the filter alone. A `MutationObserver` on the entries' `class` scrolls the wrapper into view whenever a pick leaves it above the window: a card's tag filters in place, and the shortened page clamped a reader who clicked far down to its bottom. The observer's callback runs after the click handler, so the list has already been filtered. The cloud is marked `data-vm-cloud-ready`.

**The theme is generated.** `build.mjs` reads the chrome tokens out of `src/css/tokens.css` (the light block, and the dark block over it) and fills them into `src/theme/theme.scss` twice, as `$vm-* … !default` variables and as the `--vm-*` properties they re-emit. So the Bootstrap chrome and the panels can't disagree, and a `$vm-*` override reaches both. The Bootstrap variables it derives are deliberately not `!default`: Quarto presets some of them as `!default` ahead of the theme, and a `!default` here would silently lose.

**Fonts sit flat.** `fonts.css` names each `.woff2` by bare file name, and Quarto copies a dependency's files flat into `site_libs/quarto-contrib/mathviz-fonts-<version>/`, so they land side by side. A root-relative `url(/fonts/…)` is rewritten wrongly by Quarto, which is why it isn't used; `src/fonts/fonts.test.js` checks every `url()` resolves and nothing points at Google.
